name: What is the difference between a remodel and a renovation?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between remodeling and renovating a home, and why does the distinction matter for permits and pricing?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between remodeling and renovating a home, and why does the distinction matter for permits and pricing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Renovation and remodeling are often used interchangeably, but they are not always the same in practice. Renovation usually refers to updating or restoring what is already there, such as new finishes, fixtures, flooring, paint, or cabinet replacement in the same layout. Remodeling usually means changing how a space works, which can include moving walls, relocating a kitchen sink, adding circuits, changing door openings, or redesigning room flow. That distinction matters because remodels are more likely to require plan review, permits, inspections, and a larger budget. It also affects scheduling, since redesign work often requires architectural or structural coordination before construction begins. Homeowners searching in Los Angeles-area neighborhoods often need to know this difference because permit rules and bid pricing depend more on scope than on the word used in marketing. The safest approach is to define the project by actions, not labels, so contractors and permit reviewers are discussing the same work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Renovation usually means restoring or updating existing spaces without major layout changes, while remodeling usually means altering the structure, layout, or function of a space. In practice, the term matters because moving walls, plumbing, electrical, or mechanical systems typically increases permit needs, design complexity, and cost.
